result.title: Action-Value Calibration via Continuation Sharing for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Reinforcement learning for long-horizon agents relies on feedback from sequences of interactions, making credit assignment to individual actions difficult. Existing methods such as GiGPO compare actions at shared states to compute relative advantages, but estimate each action's value from a single sampled continuation. The resulting local credit remains sensitive to decisions made later in the trajectory. To address this problem, we propose ConCal (Continuation Calibration), a recursive continuation-value estimator that incorporates continuation evidence already present in a rollout batch. ConCal matches visits from the same task by their incoming state-action-state transitions, combines shared continuation evidence with each visit's own transition estimate, and propagates calibrated values backward to refine earlier action-value estimates. This reduces dependence on individual sampled continuations and mitigates local credit distortions without additional rollouts. Held-out return diagnostics show lower error in within-group value differences and higher agreement with reference action orderings than estimates based on individual continuations. With Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, ConCal improves success rates over GiGPO by 3.39 and 5.86 percentage points on ALFWorld and WebShop, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/Yingjian-Chen/ConCal.

AI.brief_summary: 针对长程 agentic RL 中逐动作信用分配困难的问题，作者提出 ConCal：在已有 rollout batch 内按状态-动作-状态转移匹配同一任务的访问，递归合并共享的后续轨迹证据与各访问自身的估计，并将校准值反向传播以修正早期动作价值，无需额外采样。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不做视觉或多模态推理，但其「用同一批轨迹中的共享后续证据校准单条采样的价值估计」的思路，可能为 LVR 中轨迹贡献分配与推理步骤监督信号降噪提供可核查的方法线索。
